question: Who is known to have revived Bharatanatyam dance form in its modern version today?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rukmini Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** is credited with reviving Bharatanatyam, a classical dance form, from its decline during colonial rule.
 
• She redefined Bharatanatyam by removing its association with temple rituals and presenting it as a respectable art form on stage.
 
• Rukmini Devi introduced innovations such as incorporating themes from Indian mythology and epics into Bharatanatyam performances.
 
• She was the first woman to perform Bharatanatyam on stage in its modern form, breaking societal taboos of the time.
 
• In addition to her contributions to dance, Rukmini Devi was also a theosophist, animal rights activist, and a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:** A classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu that combines expression (abhinaya), melody (raga), rhythm (tala), and spiritual themes.
 
• **Devadasi System:** Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed by temple dancers called Devadasis as part of religious rituals. This practice declined during colonial rule.
 
• **Theosophy and Dance:** Rukmini Devi's involvement in the Theosophical Society influenced her vision of Bharatanatyam as a spiritual and cultural art form.
 
• **Kalakshetra Foundation:** Rukmini Devi founded this institution in Chennai to promote and teach Bharatanatyam and other traditional Indian arts.
 
• **Recognition:** Rukmini Devi received several honors, including the Padma Bhushan (1956), for her contributions to Indian art and culture.
